name: Paramo
notes: High-Andean paramo (Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador, N Peru) above cloud forest: humid, giant-rosette frailejones, tussock grasses, cushion bogs and dwarf shrubs; Espeletia in the north, Puya and Chusquea widespread.

canopy.name: Paramo polylepis
canopy.origin: Andes of Ecuador and N Peru

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings come up in moss and leaf litter under the parent trees. The young plant is a stiff sprig of compound leaves with 3-5 small, thick, dark, net-veined leaflets, felted pale beneath, crowded at the shoot tips; within a few years the stem twists and starts shedding thin red-brown papery bark.
growth.source: Kessler 1995 / Simpson 1979 Polylepis revision (P. reticulata: tree of humid paramo, Ecuador and N Peru, ~3,400-4,500 m, leathery reticulate leaflets, multilayered red peeling bark); growth rate from tree-ring work on P. reticulata in the Ecuadorian Andes (slow radial growth); ages and first seeding estimated

canopy.source: Polylepis reticulata (Kew POWO; Simpson 1979 A revision of the genus Polylepis): small twisted tree of the humid paramo of Ecuador and northern Peru, 3,400-4,500 m, forming patches and groves on sheltered slopes and rock outcrops above the cloud forest; leaflets coriaceous with deeply impressed reticulate veins above and dense pale tomentum beneath; bark of many thin red-brown papery layers.

traits.native_range: humid paramo of Ecuador and N Peru, 3400-4500 m
traits.leaf_shape: small compound leaves of thick net-veined leaflets
traits.trunk: short twisted trunk, crooked low limbs, peeling red bark
traits.petiole: short petiole with a sheathing base
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

bark.notes: dozens of thin red-brown papery layers peel and flutter from trunk and limbs

leaf.notes: leaves of 3-5 thick obovate leaflets, dark green and deeply net-veined above, felted buff below, crowded at twig tips

flower.form: pendent spikes of small green petal-less flowers with purple-red anthers

fruit.form: small hard achene with irregular wings or knobs

appearance.silhouette: crooked red-barked tree with dark leathery crown

fruiting.source: Simpson 1979 (Polylepis: wind-pollinated, petal-less flowers on pendent racemes, sepals green, anthers purple; achenes winged or spiny); equatorial flowering spread through the year estimated

canopy.silhouette: crooked red-barked tree with dark leathery crown

canopy.name: Kolle
canopy.origin: Andes of Ecuador, Peru and Bolivia

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny winged seeds germinate on bare rocky soil. The seedling bears opposite pairs of small, thick, shiny leaves, woolly beneath, and soon branches from near the ground into a dense, low, many-stemmed bush that only slowly lifts a short crooked trunk.
growth.source: Norman 2000 Flora Neotropica Buddlejaceae (B. coriacea: densely crowned sprawling shrub or tree branching near the ground, usually under 4 m, rarely 12 m; 3,000-4,350 m on dry to semi-humid rocky soils, −3 to 15 °C); growth rates and ages estimated

canopy.source: Buddleja coriacea (Kew POWO; Norman 2000 Flora Neotropica): high-Andean shrub or small tree of Ecuador, Peru and Bolivia, 3,000-4,350 m on dry to semi-humid rocky soils; leaves small, thick and leathery, 1-4 cm, glossy and waxy above, appressed-tomentose below, margins entire and often recurved; orange flowers in small heads; used with Polylepis in high-Andean woodland.

traits.native_range: high Andes of Ecuador, Peru and Bolivia, 3000-4350 m
traits.trunk: short crooked trunk branching near the ground
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

bark.notes: grey-brown bark in shallow vertical fissures, flaking in narrow strips on old stems

leaf.notes: small thick elliptic leaves in opposite pairs, glossy waxy green above, buff-felted beneath, edges rolled under

fruit.form: small brown two-valved capsules with tiny winged seeds

canopy.name: Rodamonte

growth.juvenile_note: Dust-fine seeds germinate on moist moss and bare peat. The seedling is a thin upright stem with tiny glossy obovate leaves; early on it puts out near-horizontal side branches in tiers, so even a young plant shows the flat-layered 'pagoda' outline, the leaves crowded in rosettes on short shoots along each tier.
growth.source: Colombian floras / Luteyn 1999 (E. myrtilloides: shrub or tree 2-5 m, strongly tiered pagoda-like crown, subparamo and paramo 2,500-3,900 m in Colombia, 1,900-4,200 m overall); growth rates and ages estimated

canopy.source: Escallonia myrtilloides (Kew POWO; Luteyn 1999 Paramos checklist; Flora de Costa Rica): shrub or small tree 2-5 m of subparamo and paramo from Costa Rica to Bolivia, 2,500-3,900 m in Colombia; branches in flat horizontal tiers, giving a 'Chinese pagoda' crown; small obovate crenulate leaves crowded on short shoots; small white flowers solitary at the shoot tips.

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings after a mass flowering look like thin grass. The young clump makes new culms each season, at first thread-thin and short, each generation thicker and taller, and dense bunches of whiskery branchlets grow at every node. In the paramo it forms low, very dense clumps of stiff culms clothed in overlapping straw-coloured sheaths.
growth.source: Clark 1989/1995 Chusquea studies and Paramo vegetation accounts (C. tessellata forms dense 'bamboo paramo' stands at 3000-4000 m in Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador); Chusquea often gregarious and monocarpic; cycle length, growth and culm life estimated

shrub.name: Chuquiragua
shrub.origin: Andes of Colombia, Ecuador and Peru

growth.juvenile_note: A seedling with two small cotyledons, then a stiff upright sprig densely clothed in small, hard, overlapping, spine-tipped leaves. It branches slowly from the base into a low, prickly, rounded shrub whose stem tips carry single bright orange flower heads.
growth.source: Ezcurra 1985 revision of Chuquiraga; Ecuadorian paramo floras (low shrub to ~75 cm, to 3 m on Cotopaxi; 3,000-5,000 m); growth rates and ages estimated

shrub.source: Chuquiraga jussieui (Kew POWO; Ezcurra 1985 Revision del genero Chuquiraga): 'flower of the Andes', national flower of Ecuador; low rigid shrub of grass and rocky paramo of Colombia, Ecuador and Peru, 3,000-5,000 m; leaves small, coriaceous, imbricate and spine-tipped; solitary terminal heads of orange-yellow tubular florets visited by hillstar hummingbirds.

shrub.name: Andean blueberry

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny seeds germinate on moist peat and moss. The seedling has small glossy oval leaves, bronze-red when new, and soon sends several thin wiry stems up from a woody base, becoming a low twiggy evergreen bush that later layers along the ground.
growth.source: Mortino reviews (Vasco et al. 2009; Coba et al. 2022): evergreen shrub 0.2-2.5 m, often prostrate or scandent, edges of humid paramo 3,000-4,500 m; growth rates and ages estimated

shrub.source: Vaccinium floribundum (Kew POWO; Luteyn 1999 Paramos checklist): mortino, evergreen shrub of the humid paramo and upper montane forest from Venezuela to Bolivia, 1,600-4,500 m, most common 3,000-4,500 m; leaves small, glossy, crenate-serrulate, reddish when young; pink to red urn-shaped flowers in racemes of 6-10; blue-black berries 5-8 mm, eaten and gathered.

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny seedlings with two round cotyledons, then pairs of narrow, needle-like leaves; young plants are wiry little sprigs with crowded, larch-like needles on reddish stems. They branch densely into a rounded, heath-like shrublet dotted with golden-yellow, five-petalled flowers at the branch tips.
growth.source: Hypericum online monograph (N. Robson, illustration of H. laricifolium, Ecuador and Venezuela); Wikipedia; growth, germination and ages estimated from Andean Hypericum sect. Brathys shrubs and paramo shrub growth rates.

fruiting.source: Estimated from Hypericum sect. Brathys (solitary or few golden 5-petalled flowers at branch tips, dry septicidal capsules, tiny seeds) and paramo pollination studies (bumblebees and flies); flowering spread through the year in the equatorial Andes.

ground.name: Sphagnum moss

growth.juvenile_note: A spore germinates into a tiny flat green plate that buds leafy shoots. The young colony is a soft cushion of fat, blunt, wine-red to purplish capitula (greener in shade) with swollen, spoon-shaped leaves, growing 1-3 cm taller a year in wet lawns and spreading into a spongy carpet.
growth.source: Springer Wetl. Ecol. Manag. 2019 (Chiloe, Chile: ~5.6 mm growth in 3 months, ~2 cm/yr); Diaz et al. 2012 Rev. Chil. Hist. Nat. (growth higher in lawns than hummocks); Bengtsson et al. 2016 (magellanicum-group 1-7 mm/yr in Sweden); shading aids regeneration (Can. J. Bot. 2025)

repro.note: spores by wind and water; no flowers; needs a wet film to reproduce, so spread reads moisture not pollinators

ground.source: Bogs worldwide; holds twenty times its weight in water and makes the peat; red in the open, green in shade. Kew POWO.

ground.name: Paramo club moss
ground.source: Lycopodium clavatum, cosmopolitan incl. Andean paramo, trailing club moss 5-20 cm

traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

growth.juvenile_note: Spores germinate underground into a tiny non-green, fungus-fed gametophyte that takes years (often 6-15) to mature, so the value above is capped. The sporeling is one small upright shoot densely clad in tiny needle-like scale leaves; it then sends a creeping runner over the ground that roots and throws up forked, bristly upright shoots. Spore cones on long stalks come ~4-6 yr later.
growth.source: USDA Forest Service GTR NC-217 'Lycopodium: growth form, morphology and sustainability' (spore-gametophyte-sporophyte cycle up to 20 yr; gametophytes live weeks to 10+ yr; aerial stems produce spores at 4-6 yr; ramets 1-6 yr old); Bruchmann/Whittier on subterranean mycoheterotrophic gametophytes

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds sprout on bare, wet paramo soil or among mosses. The seedling is a small tuft of stiff, inrolled, needle-like leaves; over years it builds a dense, knee-high tussock of tough grey-green leaves around a core of dead leaf bases that insulates the growing buds against nightly frost.
growth.source: Estimated from paramo tussock-grass ecology (C. effusa is a dominant bunchgrass of the northern Andean paramos, forming dense tussocks insulated by dead leaves); no species growth data found.

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: a tiny tuft of short, stiff, two-ranked leaves a few millimetres long. Shoots branch and pack side by side into a small, hard, flat-topped, bright green cushion that spreads into sheets over the wet ground of high-Andean bogs; dead lower shoots build up underneath as peat, so the living surface rises a few cm a year.
growth.source: Wikipedia Distichia muscoides (cushion of densely packed evergreen shoots and mm-long leaves forming a firm flat surface; growth up to 5 cm/yr in favourable sites; dominates Andean bofedales over peat up to 5 m thick; year-round grazing). Germination, first flowering and cushion age estimated.

ground.name: Paramo sphagnum
ground.origin: Costa Rica and the northern Andes

growth.juvenile_note: Spores sprout into a small flat thalloid protonema on wet peat, which sends up the first leafy shoots; each shoot ends in a dense head of short branches, and shoots packed side by side build a spongy carpet that grows up a few cm a year while the base dies to peat.
growth.source: Crum & Crosby 1974 Ann. Missouri Bot. Gard. (described from high Costa Rica); Colombian high-Andean peatland surveys (a dominant of disturbed high peatlands, Cundinamarca); carpet growth and ages from Sphagnum in general, estimated

repro.note: spores by wind from capsules shot off the capitulum; spreads mainly by fragments and branching shoots in the wet carpet

ground.source: Sphagnum sancto-josephense H.A.Crum & Crosby (Tropicos; Crum & Crosby 1974): peat moss described from high-altitude Costa Rica, one of the commonest Sphagnum there and a carpet-former in high Andean peatlands of Colombia, dominant on disturbed sites; colour estimated from the genus.

traits.native_range: peat bogs of high Costa Rica and the Colombian Andes
traits.note: leaf/trunk/petiole derived from the plant's shape class; per-species detail where the entry carries it (aroids, cannabis)

ground.name: Coral lichen
ground.origin: Tropical mountains and the southern hemisphere

growth.juvenile_note: Begins as a crust of tiny granules on bare soil or rock; upright grey-white stalks rise from it, covered in small coral-like branchlets, and grow into loose tufts a few cm tall tipped with dark brown fruit discs.
growth.source: Colombian Stereocaulon revision (pseudopodetia over 20 mm, sparsely branched above, cylindrical phyllocladia, abundant red-brown to black apothecia; paramos of Colombia and Ecuador); growth rate estimated from the genus

repro.note: spores from the dark apothecia by wind; also spreads by broken fragments of the stalks

ground.source: Stereocaulon ramulosum Raeusch. (Index Fungorum): terricolous fruticose lichen of cool, cloudy, wet mountains, widely spread in the southern hemisphere and tropical mountains; in the paramos of Colombia and Ecuador; grey-white pseudopodetia over 20 mm with coral-like phyllocladia and large dark brown apothecia.
